title: Dataset of intracranial EEG during cortical stimulation evoking visual effects
description: Intracranial EEG (stereo-EEG) recordings from 22 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy undergoing presurgical evaluation, capturing responses to 115 high-frequency intracranial electrical stimulations that evoked visual hallucinations. Each recording spans 21 seconds around the stimulation, with events annotated by stimulated contact pair, current intensity, and evoked effect, classified into 14 clinical categories. The data support identification of brain networks underlying visual symptoms and creation of symptom-related activation and connectivity maps.
methods_description: High-frequency bipolar stimulation was delivered through intracranial contacts using alternating-polarity biphasic pulses of 1 ms duration at 43.2 or 50 Hz, with current intensity of 0.25 to 3 mA for up to 5 s. Each epoch includes 8 s before stimulation, up to 5 s of stimulation, and 8 s after stimulation. The alternating-polarity protocol allows neuronal responses time-locked to pulses to be separated from stimulation artefacts.
